whoIsThisFor.heading: Who should take the CRM Analytics and Einstein Discovery Consultant exam?

personas.label: CRM Analytics practitioners
personas.description: You build datasets and dashboards and want to show that you understand data preparation, access controls, and predictions.

personas.label: Salesforce administrators responsible for analytics
personas.description: Your team needs more than standard reports, and you support CRM Analytics work in Salesforce.

personas.label: Analytics implementation consultants
personas.description: You scope or deliver analytics solutions and need to plan for security, model quality, and deployment.

examDifficulty.heading: How challenging is the CRM Analytics and Einstein Discovery Consultant exam?
examDifficulty.summary: The exam spans CRM Analytics data preparation and dashboards as well as Einstein Discovery models and predictions. Security design and model evaluation require careful study because they involve decisions beyond simply building a chart.
bullets: 60 questions. Check the current exam guide for the time limit and testing details.
65% passing score. Confirm the current requirement before scheduling.
Access controls matter: Understand security predicates and when a dataset can inherit Salesforce sharing.
Evaluate models before deployment: Review model metrics, potential leakage, and bias checks.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Practice writing an access rule for a specific dataset and explain when inherited sharing may be suitable. Also review a Discovery model, assess its metrics, and check for leakage or bias before deciding whether it is ready to deploy.

examFormat.heading: CRM Analytics and Einstein Discovery Consultant exam format
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or at a test center. Questions cover data preparation, dashboard behavior, security, and predictive analytics.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Many questions describe an analytics requirement and ask which feature best supports it. Compare solutions by their behavior and maintenance needs, such as using a recipe for data preparation or inherited sharing when the goal is to respect Salesforce sharing.
bestWayToPass: Build a data preparation flow: Load, join, transform, and output data so you understand how recipes and dataflows differ.
Practice security design: Work through owner-based and role-based examples, and understand what each security approach can express.
Create and assess a Discovery story: Review model metrics and check for leakage and bias before deployment.
Learn dashboard interactions: Understand how selection and results bindings pass values between widgets, and when SAQL is needed.

certificationCard.description: Covers CRM Analytics data preparation, datasets, dashboards, row-level access, and Einstein Discovery stories, model evaluation, and predictions on Salesforce records. The exam is 60 scored questions in 90 minutes, with a 65% pass mark, weighted towards Data Layer (23%) and Analytics Dashboard Implementation (19%).

keyConcepts.h2: CRM Analytics and Einstein Discovery: core concepts

blocks.heading: Datasets, Dataflows, and Recipes
blocks.body: CRM Analytics dashboards and lenses query datasets. A dataset is prepared data that is refreshed through a data preparation process rather than a live view of Salesforce records. Dataflows define preparation steps in a JSON-based format. Recipes provide a visual way to join and transform data, with previews along the way. Common dataflow operations include digesting Salesforce data, augmenting a dataset with related columns, flattening hierarchical data, and registering an output dataset. Choose the preparation tool that fits the requirement and the org’s established approach.

blocks.heading: Lenses, Dashboards, and Bindings
blocks.body: A lens explores one dataset. A dashboard combines visualizations and other widgets. Bindings pass a value from one widget or query to another. A selection binding uses a user selection; a results binding uses query output. Pages can organize dashboard views. For performance and clarity, limit unnecessary queries and filter data close to where it is prepared or queried. Faceting can coordinate filters across related widgets.

blocks.heading: Einstein Discovery Stories and Models
blocks.body: An Einstein Discovery story analyzes a dataset in relation to an outcome and highlights factors associated with that outcome. Review the model metrics that fit the outcome type: numeric predictions can be evaluated with measures such as R-squared and mean absolute error; classification models can be evaluated with a confusion matrix and related measures. Metrics are only part of the review. Check whether an input variable reveals information that would not be available when a prediction is made, and use bias checks to assess differences across relevant groups before deployment.

blocks.heading: Deploying Predictions to Salesforce
blocks.body: A prediction definition connects a model to a Salesforce object so scores and related insights can be used in the business process. Deployment requires mapping model variables to fields available on the target object. Predictions may be evaluated as a user works with a record or applied to records in bulk, depending on the setup. A prediction can also be used in Flow to support an automated follow-up. Know how the model inputs map to the target data and how the score will be used.

blocks.heading: Row-Level Security
blocks.body: CRM Analytics datasets need an explicit access design. A security predicate filters dataset rows using dataset fields and user information. For example, an owner-based rule can compare the row owner with the current user. Hierarchy requirements may need a flattened hierarchy field or another representation suitable for the predicate. Inherited sharing can align dataset access with sharing on the source Salesforce object where supported. Choose based on the access requirement, source data, supported scale, and maintenance needs; do not assume that dataset access automatically mirrors Salesforce record access.

scenarioTips.h2: How to prepare for the CRM Analytics and Einstein Discovery Consultant exam
scenarioTips.intro: For each scenario, identify whether it concerns data preparation, dashboard interaction, row access, model evaluation, or prediction deployment. Then choose the feature that meets the requirement and can be maintained.

blocks.heading: Choose Recipes or Dataflows
blocks.body: Understand how both tools prepare data, and review the common dataflow operations. For a new preparation flow, know the capabilities of the visual recipe experience.

blocks.heading: Write and Review Security Rules
blocks.body: Practice owner-based and hierarchy-based access examples. Be able to explain when an explicit predicate is needed and when inherited sharing may fit.

blocks.heading: Assess the Model Before Deployment
blocks.body: Use appropriate metrics for the prediction type, check for leakage, and assess bias across relevant groups before publishing a model.

blocks.heading: Know the Binding Types
blocks.body: Selection bindings use a user’s selection; results bindings use query results. Build a small example of each to learn how one widget can affect another.

blocks.heading: Map and Use Predictions
blocks.body: When deploying a prediction, map the model variables to fields on the Salesforce object and decide whether users, bulk processing, or Flow will consume the score.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Related credentials after CRM Analytics and Einstein Discovery
nextCertsAfter.intro: Build on analytics skills with a Salesforce platform credential or a role-focused consultant certification.

sampleQuestions.question: A dataset should show each user only rows they own. Which approach directly filters the rows by the current user?
options: A dashboard-level owner filter
Remove the dataset from every app
An owner-based security predicate
Field-level security on the source object
sampleQuestions.explanation: A security predicate can compare the row owner value with the current user and restrict dataset rows accordingly.
whyWrong: A dashboard filter affects a particular view and is not a dataset-wide access rule.
Removing the dataset prevents use rather than providing owner-based row access.
Field-level security controls access to fields, not which dataset rows a user can see.

sampleQuestions.question: The requirement is for dataset access to follow existing Salesforce object sharing, and the data volume is moderate. What should be considered first?
options: Inherited sharing on the dataset
No row restriction because app access is sufficient
A separate dataset for every role
A hand-written predicate that duplicates the sharing model
sampleQuestions.explanation: Inherited sharing can use access from the underlying Salesforce object when the dataset setup supports it.
whyWrong: This directly matches the goal of respecting the source object sharing model.
App access alone does not necessarily restrict which rows a user can query.
Duplicating datasets by role increases maintenance and is not required by this scenario.

sampleQuestions.question: A Discovery model has strong accuracy, but one input field is populated only after the outcome is known. What should the team do?
options: Deploy because the accuracy score is high
Remove the field and retrain
Convert the field to text and keep it
Deploy and document the limitation
sampleQuestions.explanation: A field that reveals information unavailable at prediction time can leak the outcome; remove it and retrain before judging the model again.
whyWrong: Strong metrics do not make a model valid if it uses information from after the outcome.
Changing the field type does not remove the information leakage.
Documentation does not correct a model that relies on an unavailable future value.

sampleQuestions.question: Which dataflow operation adds matching columns from one dataset to another?
options: Augment
sfdcDigest
sfdcRegister
Flatten
sampleQuestions.explanation: Augment joins related columns from another dataset based on matching key fields.
whyWrong: Digest extracts Salesforce object data into the data preparation flow.
Register writes the prepared output as a dataset.
Flatten changes hierarchical data into a form that can be queried.

sampleQuestions.question: A dashboard widget should use the result of another query, rather than a value the user clicked. Which binding is appropriate?
options: A results binding
A security predicate
A new dataset
A selection binding
sampleQuestions.explanation: A results binding passes output from one query to another widget or query.
whyWrong: A security predicate limits data access and does not connect query results between widgets.
A separate dataset is not necessary just to pass one query’s result.
A selection binding responds to user selections rather than query output.

sampleQuestions.question: Which tool is a visual option for preparing and transforming data in CRM Analytics?
options: A report snapshot
An Apex batch job
A JSON dataflow
A recipe in Data Prep
sampleQuestions.explanation: Recipes provide a visual data preparation workflow with transformation steps and previews.
whyWrong: A report snapshot is not the CRM Analytics data preparation tool described here.
Apex can process data in custom code but is not the visual recipe interface.
Dataflows are JSON-defined; the question asks for the visual preparation tool.

sampleQuestions.question: A deployed score should create a follow-up task when it falls below a chosen threshold. What can automate that response?
options: Ask users to check the score and create tasks manually
Add a formula to the dashboard
Use the prediction in a Flow
Retrain the model with a different threshold
sampleQuestions.explanation: Flow can consume a prediction and create an action, such as a follow-up task, when conditions are met.
whyWrong: Manual review does not automate the requested follow-up.
A dashboard formula does not itself create Salesforce tasks.
Changing the model threshold is not the same as automating a task from the score.

sampleQuestions.question: Which dataflow operation can make a role hierarchy usable as dataset columns for filtering?
options: Flatten
Augment
dim2mea
Slice
sampleQuestions.explanation: Flatten can turn hierarchical data into columns that can be queried or used in a predicate.
whyWrong: Augment joins related columns but does not itself convert a hierarchy to flat rows.
dim2mea changes a dimension into a measure; it does not represent a role hierarchy.
Slice is not the dataflow operation described for flattening hierarchical relationships.

sampleQuestions.question: Which measures are suitable when evaluating a model that predicts a numeric value such as deal amount?
options: Precision and recall
A confusion matrix
R-squared and mean absolute error
The number of insights produced
sampleQuestions.explanation: R-squared and mean absolute error are examples of metrics used to evaluate numeric predictions.
whyWrong: Precision and recall are generally used for classification outcomes.
A confusion matrix summarizes classification results rather than numeric prediction error.
The count of insights does not measure the accuracy of numeric predictions.

sampleQuestions.question: Why can adding many widgets make a CRM Analytics dashboard slower?
options: The server must render each widget in a strict sequence
Each widget can add another dataset query
A new dataset is created for every widget
Predicates run only once for each user session
sampleQuestions.explanation: More widgets can mean more queries and requests, increasing the work needed to load the dashboard.
whyWrong: Widgets do not necessarily render in a strict sequence on the server.
Dataset count does not automatically increase with each dashboard widget.
This does not describe how predicates cause dashboard loading delays.

sampleQuestions.question: A Discovery dataset includes a sensitive field such as gender. What should the team do before deployment?
options: Assume the model is objective because it is data-driven
Delete the entire dataset
Run bias checks across relevant groups
Convert the field into a measure
sampleQuestions.explanation: Bias checks can help the team evaluate whether model results differ across relevant groups before deployment.
whyWrong: Models can reproduce or amplify patterns in their training data; objectivity should not be assumed.
Deleting the dataset is unnecessary if the team can assess and govern the feature appropriately.
Changing the field type does not assess whether predictions differ across groups.

sampleQuestions.question: How does a CRM Analytics dataset relate to Salesforce records?
options: It is a Salesforce report type
A scheduled snapshot of prepared data
It queries Salesforce live whenever a dashboard opens
It is a live database view
sampleQuestions.explanation: A dataset contains prepared data that is refreshed through its data preparation process rather than acting as a live view.
whyWrong: A report type is a separate Salesforce reporting configuration.
A dataset is not automatically a live query of Salesforce each time a dashboard opens.
The dataset is prepared output, not a live database view.

sampleQuestions.question: A prediction definition will be deployed to the Opportunity object. Which setup step is essential?
options: Add a results binding to the object
Map model variables to fields on the object
Write a security predicate for the model
Create a new dataflow
sampleQuestions.explanation: The model inputs must be mapped to fields available on the target Salesforce object for scoring.
whyWrong: Bindings connect dashboard queries and widgets; they do not map model inputs to object fields.
A predicate controls dataset row access and is not the prediction field mapping.
A new dataflow may not be required to deploy a prediction definition.

sampleQuestions.question: When is writing SAQL directly a reasonable choice?
options: For every dashboard widget
To replace recipes for all data preparation
Whenever a dashboard has performance issues
When the builder cannot express the query
sampleQuestions.explanation: SAQL is useful when the required query or calculation is not available through the builder controls.
whyWrong: Many dashboard widgets can be built without hand-written SAQL.
Recipes prepare data and are not replaced by SAQL for all preparation work.
Performance problems need diagnosis; custom SAQL is not automatically the solution.

sampleQuestions.question: A manager should see rows for everyone below them in a role hierarchy. Which approach can support this requirement?
options: Field-level security on the role field
A dashboard filter on manager name
A separate dashboard for each manager
A flattened role field with a predicate
sampleQuestions.explanation: A flattened hierarchy field can be combined with a predicate to express which rows fall under the running user.
whyWrong: Field-level security controls field visibility, not row-level hierarchy access.
A dashboard filter does not provide a complete dataset access rule.
Separate dashboards add maintenance and do not enforce the underlying row access.

sampleQuestions.question: A company wants to turn on CRM Analytics for a group of users, but not for everyone in the org. What should the consultant check first?
options: Permission sets and licenses that control who gets CRM Analytics access
The org's Salesforce edition alone
The number of custom objects in the org
The Lightning theme applied to the org
sampleQuestions.explanation: Enabling CRM Analytics for a specific group of users depends on assigning the right permission sets and licenses to those users, not a blanket org-wide switch.
whyWrong: Salesforce edition can gate feature availability generally, but it doesn't control which specific users get access.
The number of custom objects has nothing to do with who can use CRM Analytics.
A Lightning theme is a visual setting, unrelated to feature access.

sampleQuestions.question: A team has built dataflows, recipes, and dashboards in a sandbox and now needs to move them to production. What should they plan for?
options: A deployment process between environments, since CRM Analytics assets don't move automatically
Nothing, sandbox and production always share the same CRM Analytics assets
Manually retyping every SAQL query in production
Assets can only ever be built directly in production
sampleQuestions.explanation: Moving CRM Analytics assets from sandbox to production requires a deliberate deployment/migration process between environments, assets don't sync automatically.
whyWrong: Sandbox and production are separate environments with separate CRM Analytics assets.
A proper deployment process avoids the error-prone work of manually rebuilding queries.
Building directly in production skips the safe build-and-test workflow the exam expects.

sampleQuestions.question: A business wants a working CRM Analytics app for standard sales metrics without building every dashboard and dataflow from scratch. What should the consultant use?
options: A standard CRM Analytics templated app, configured to fit the business's needs
A blank app with every object imported manually
A single widget pasted into a Salesforce page
A Flow that generates reports
sampleQuestions.explanation: A standard templated app (like Sales Analytics) comes with pre-built dataflows, datasets, and dashboards for a common use case, and the consultant configures it to match specific requirements instead of starting from zero.
whyWrong: Manually importing every object from scratch ignores the time-saving purpose of templated apps.
A single widget doesn't deliver a full analytics app.
Flow automates business processes, it doesn't build a CRM Analytics app.

sampleQuestions.question: Before building any dashboard, a consultant meets with stakeholders to confirm what questions the dashboard must answer and which of those matter most. What is this process called?
options: Scoping, validating, and prioritizing dashboard design requirements
Writing SAQL queries immediately
Picking a random dashboard template
Skipping requirements and building based on guesswork
sampleQuestions.explanation: Good dashboard design starts with scoping, validating, and prioritizing the business requirements before any build work begins, following CRM Analytics best practices.
whyWrong: Writing SAQL is an implementation step that comes later, not the upfront requirements process.
Picking a template without scoping requirements risks building the wrong thing.
Skipping requirements gathering is exactly what best practices warn against.

sampleQuestions.question: A dashboard has grown slow to load after several widgets were added. Which tool should the consultant use to find and fix the bottleneck?
options: Dashboard Inspector
A new dataset with the same data duplicated
Field-level security
A permission set
sampleQuestions.explanation: Dashboard Inspector shows query execution details per widget, letting a consultant monitor and optimize dashboard performance.
whyWrong: Duplicating the dataset adds overhead and doesn't diagnose the actual bottleneck.
Field-level security controls field visibility, it has nothing to do with dashboard load performance.
A permission set controls access, not query performance.
